raw.description: Sensitive information such as JWT secret is loaded from environment variables without validation or encryption.
raw.exploit: An attacker with access to the environment variables can retrieve the JWT secret and forge tokens.

raw.description: CSRF protection is not implemented for state-changing requests like login.
raw.exploit: An attacker can trick a user into making unwanted requests to the application by exploiting the user's authenticated session.

raw.description: Improper access control in the '/api/projects' endpoint allows users to view projects they do not own if they are not an admin.
raw.exploit: A non-admin user can potentially access projects they do not own by manipulating the request.

raw.description: Improper access control in the '/api/projects/:id' endpoint allows users to delete projects without verifying ownership.
raw.exploit: An attacker can delete projects they do not own by sending a DELETE request with the project ID.

raw.description: Potential XSS vulnerability if project names are not properly sanitized before rendering.
raw.exploit: An attacker can inject malicious scripts into project names, which will execute when viewed by other users.

raw.description: Hardcoded secrets are not present, but reliance on environment variables without validation can lead to insecure configurations.
raw.exploit: If environment variables are not properly set, the application may use default or insecure values.
